translationRepairs: Back at court he was made secure-the-front general and supernumerary bearer of the left secondary insignia.
Back at court he was made secure-the-front general and Right Grand Master with Splendid Happiness.

s0031 還為安前將軍、右光祿大夫 names 右光祿大夫, the Right Guanglu office; the English invents a left secondary-insignia title and misreads 右 as left, while Right Grand Master with Splendid Happiness restores the office.
Returning, he was made secure-the-front general and supernumerary bearer of the left secondary insignia.
Returning, he was made secure-the-front general and Right Grand Master with Splendid Happiness.
s0031 右光祿大夫 is Right Guanglu Dafu; the literal's left secondary-insignia wording is unsupported, and Right Grand Master with Splendid Happiness matches the Chinese office.
Shipu's younger cousin Shiuxiu followed him on Liang campaigns and won merit in battle.
Shipu's younger cousin Shixiu followed him on Liang campaigns and won merit in battle.
s0035 世譜從弟世休 gives the personal name 世休, romanized Shixiu; Shiuxiu inserts an extra syllable not in the Chinese.
Shipu's younger cousin Shiuxiu followed Shipu on Liang punitive campaigns and also had battle merit.
Shipu's younger cousin Shixiu followed Shipu on Liang punitive campaigns and also had battle merit.
s0035 世休 is Shixiu; the literal's Shiuxiu is the same typographical extra syllable and Shixiu corrects it without other change.
When the Founder took the throne, Wang Lin held the upper Yangzi. Yu Xiaoxiang with Lin's ally Li
When the Founder took the throne, Wang Lin held the upper Yangzi. Yu Xiaoqing with Lin's ally Li
s0081 余孝頃 is Yu Xiaoqing (孝頃); Xiaoxiang misreads 頃 and is not supported by the Chinese.
When the Founder received the abdication, Wang Lin held the upper Yangzi; Yu Xiaoxiang with Lin's partisan Li
When the Founder received the abdication, Wang Lin held the upper Yangzi; Yu Xiaoqing with Lin's partisan Li
s0081 余孝頃 romanizes as Yu Xiaoqing; the literal's Yu Xiaoxiang invents a different given name from 頃.
Zhou Jiong, courtesy name Wenzhao, was from Ancheng in Ruyang.
Zhou Jiong, courtesy name Wenzhao, was from Ancheng in Runan.
s0139 汝南安成人也 places him in Runan (汝南); Ruyang would be 汝陽 and is not in the text.
Zhou Jiong, style name Wenzhao, was a native of Ancheng in Ruyang.
Zhou Jiong, style name Wenzhao, was a native of Ancheng in Runan.
s0139 汝南 is Runan; the literal's Ruyang misreads the commandery name, and Ancheng in Runan restores it.
When Wang Sengbian marched east, Lang sent his general Fan Baosheng and his younger brother Xiao, each with two thousand men, to help.
When Wang Sengbian marched east, Lang sent his general Fan Baosheng and his younger brother Xiao, with two thousand men, to help.
s0115 范寶勝及弟曉領兵二千助之 has one 領兵二千 for the joint subject; each with two thousand invents a distributive reading not marked in the Chinese, and with two thousand men is accurate.
Earlier Tian Longsheng, inspector of Dingzhou under Xiao Cha, had surrendered his city;

Earlier Tian Longsheng, inspector of Dingzhou under Xiao Cha, had surrendered his city; an edict made him General Who Invigorates the Distant and inspector of Dingzhou, and enfeoffed him as Prince of Chiting.
s0167 continues after the surrender with 詔以為振遠將軍、定州刺史，封赤亭王; the idiomatic truncates those appointments, and the proposed completion restores them.

Earlier, Xiao Cha's Inspector of Dingzhou Tian Longsheng had surrendered his city; an edict appointed him General Who Invigorates the Distant and Inspector of Dingzhou, and enfeoffed him as Prince of Chiting.
s0167 詔以為振遠將軍、定州刺史，封赤亭王 follows the surrender; the literal likewise stops early, and the proposed appointment and enfeoffment wording restores the omitted Chinese.
but when Jiong came to court, Longsheng rebelled with six prefectures and seven garrisons north of the river and defected to Qi, which sent Prince Jing'an of Liyang with an army to aid him.
but when Jiong came to court, Longsheng rebelled with six prefectures and seven garrisons north of the river and defected to Qi, which sent the Prince of Liyang, Gao Jing'an, with an army to aid him.
s0168 歷陽王高景安 is the Prince of Liyang, Gao Jing'an; Prince Jing'an of Liyang wrongly folds personal name 景安 into the title.
